label: May 11–17
title: “Beware Lest Thou Forget the Lord” —  Deuteronomy 6–8; 15; 18; 29

items.text: Moses’s life was spent preparing the children of Israel not just for wilderness survival or conquering enemies, but for learning to love God, obey Him, and remain loyal. This preparation is essential for us to enter the promised land of eternal life.

The Lord is concerned about our inward state—the spiritual condition of our hearts. Reading Deuteronomy can serve as a spiritual checkup, prompting us to examine our hearts and prescribe treatments to improve our spiritual health and draw closer to Him.

The greatest commandment is to 'Love the Lord thy God with all thine heart.' This love should be a guiding principle, influencing all our thoughts, actions, and desires, leading us to obey His will and remain faithful.

Moses knew that future generations would need to remember God’s miracles and laws to remain His people. We too must remember the great things God has done for us and keep His word daily in our hearts to stay on His covenant path.

When we are instructed to 'beware lest thou forget the Lord,' it is a reminder to actively recall His blessings and teachings. This remembrance helps us to maintain our faith and devotion, especially during times of ease and prosperity.

Helping people in need requires generous hands and willing hearts. We learn from the Lord’s example to open our hands wide and to approach service with a Christlike attitude, recognizing that all blessings come from Him.

The prophecy that God would raise up a Prophet 'like unto' Moses points to Jesus Christ. We must listen to and obey Him, for He is the ultimate mediator and the source of salvation for all who believe.

The Lord desires that we choose life and obedience. He has set before us good and evil, blessing and cursing. By choosing to love Him, obey His voice, and cleave unto Him, we ensure eternal life and joy.

When we consider the goodness and greatness of God, we are inspired to keep His commandments. His love and power are demonstrated in countless ways, inviting us to draw near to Him and experience His abundant blessings.

We are reminded to pass our faith in Christ to future generations. By teaching them about the great things God has done and by living covenantal lives, we help preserve the voice of the covenant people and secure their spiritual heritage.
